40,000 participants will take part in the 42km Sydney Marathon event and major roads in North Sydney, the Sydney CBD, Pyrmont, Darlinghurst, Moore Park, Centennial Park and Kingsford will be closed between 2am and 4.30pm.

Travel across the city will be very limited with lengthy detours in place. Sydneysiders are urged to avoid non-essential travel where possible or allow plenty of extra travel time and expect trips to take longer than usual.

Key closure times by suburb area

  • North Sydney closures between 2am and 12pm including sections of Miller St and Pacific Hwy. Access Warringah Fwy via Falcon St/Military Rd.
  • Sydney Harbour Bridge, Cahill Exp and Western Distributor closed 3am to 11am. Detour via Harbour Tunnel. Motorists from the Anzac Bridge will be diverted via Bathurst St or Cross City Tunnel. Access to the Harbour Tunnel northbound is via the Cross City Tunnel only.
  • Sydney CBD, Circular Quay closures from 4am to 12pm (Macquarie St closed until 4.30pm). No access from Cahill Exp to Macquarie St until 4.30pm.
  • Millers Point, King St Wharf, Barangaroo and The Rocks closures between 4am and 11.30am.
  • Pyrmont and Ultimo closures between 4am and 11am.
  • Sydney CBD east including Macquarie St and The Domain closures between 4am and 4.30pm (Park St closed 5am to 3.30pm). No east/west crossing on surface roads available in city north - use Cross City Tunnel.
  • Sydney CBD, Darlinghurst to Moore Park closures including Oxford St and Flinders St from 4am to 4pm
  • Moore Park and Centennial Park closures from 5am to 3.30pm including parts of Moore Park Rd, Lang Rd and Anzac Pde. Centennial Park will be closed for the full 24 hour day on Sunday.
  • South East, Moore Park to Kingsford closures from 5am to 2pm including parts of Anzac Pde, while Dacey Ave and Alison Rd closed until 1.30pm - delays are expected in the Eastern Distributor while these closures are in place. The Eastern Distributor Anzac Pde entry and exit will be closed until 2pm, however the Bondi Moore Park Rd exit will remain open.
  • For detailed local area maps and managed access arrangements see the TCS Sydney Marathon website or our interactive web map.
  • Cycleways across the city will also be closed, see our cyclist detour map.

Detours:

Motorists will only be able to travel east/west across the course via the Cross City Tunnel which will be toll-free from 5am to 4.30pm or on surface roads via Gardeners Rd, Bunnerong Rd and Maroubra Rd in the South East. From 1.30pm motorists can also use Dacey Ave/Alison Rd to travel east or west across the course. See our detour map.

Widespread special event clearway parking restrictions will also be in effect along and surrounding the course. Motorists and residents should check signs carefully on the day and on Saturday night as clearways come into effect from 12.01am Sunday morning.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. AFL: Sydney Swans v Brisbane Lions at the SCG. First bounce at 3.15pm, full time at 5.55pm.

With up to 40,000 footy fans attending, significant traffic delays are expected on roads approaching Moore Park.

Motorists should allow plenty of extra travel time on roads including the Eastern Distributor, Moore Park Rd, Cleveland St, Anzac Pde and Lang Rd.

Attendees are urged to catch public transport and leave the car at home to avoid traffic delays and the high demand for parking.

Changed traffic conditions:

  • Driver Avenue will be partially closed outside the stadium from 12.15pm and will reopen once crowds have safely cleared the area.  
  • No through-traffic will be available on Driver Avenue, however access to EP2 Kippax car park will be maintained via Moore Park Road and access to EP3 grass car park and drop-off areas will be maintained from Lang Road. Grass car parks open from 12.15pm. 
  • Special event clearways will be in place on roads in Moore Park and surrounding areas from 11am to 8pm on sections of Albion Street, Fitzroy Street and Lang Road, and from 6am to 8pm on Cleveland Street.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types, and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.
